pr_title: *: Consistent Error/Warning handling for SeriesSet iterator: Allowing Async Select
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Kemal Akkoyun <kakkoyun@gmail.com>

As discussed in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/7198, this PR attempts to fix https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6878, using deferred SeriesSet iterator.

Currently, Prometheus executes PromQL “.Select” queries sequentially. Particularly for the remote storages, this implementation wastes CPU cycles while waiting for independent queries.

Requirements that gathered from the comments of https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6878 and https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/6887.

#### Requirements
* Should NOT use all the available CPU.
  * Limit concurrency
* PromQL should not care about how the querier is implemented, it should always be the same logic.
* Should avoid introducing changes to LOCAL storage.
* Should avoid spawning goroutines if there is just a single selector.

#### Changes
This PR fulfils the requirements listed above by introducing changes to `storage.SeriesSet`, `storage.Querier`, `promql/engine` and `storage/remote`.
* Add `Warnings()` to `storage.SeriesSet` https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/commit/18dddfb771f0a8711e9158dc624bd8d18beaf544
* Only return `storage.SeriesSet` from `storage.Querier.Select()` https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/commit/354a74630056f5b58251376eb96888cc22f1d1c5
* Modify `promql/engine` to propogate errors at evaluation stage. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/commit/72203b0f7b29bb83fa5716ae026cd576428039da
* And adds async implementation of SeriesSet to remote reads https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/commit/1c28c9fb31ee4dee5c4a54f204436c9d2c1e815e

This PR could be separated into smaller PRs if needed.

#### TODO
* [ ] Benchmarks

issue_context.title: promql: Add support for .Select calls concurrency.
issue_context.body:
Hi (again) Prometheus family :wave: 

## Proposal

We noticed with @brancz during our investigations on query latency that `Select` calls done by PromQL are done sequentially: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6950331/75368505-c9705e00-58b9-11ea-9313-9a8c126aa819.png)

It appears that those are subqueries required for the main (quite complex) instant query. Looks like they are done sequentially, where in our opinion they could be done concurrently. 
We would like to propose:

* Running independent subqueries in different goroutines.
* Controlled by some `subqueryMaxConcurrency` flag.

Would that make sense or lack of concurrency here is intended?

**Use case. Why is this important?**
* We are just waiting on one subquery to finish to start another independent subquery. We just waste time, CPU / Resources. We could do those asynchronously.  

cc @roidelapluie @slrtbtfs @brian-brazil @beorn7

The one thing to watch for is needlessly spawning goroutines, we never need this for local storage for example. A traffic spike to a remote system could also cause it issues.

Yes, that's why something like max concurrency flag maybe make sense?
 
And even with this, the remote system should have it's own concurrency limit logics I guess.

Anyway.. looks like it's OK to start some PR for it?
